spec.title: Sum CLI
spec.goal: Build a Rust command-line tool that sums one or more decimal integers given as arguments, prints the total, and supports `--help` and `--version`; it prints a short usage message with a non-zero exit when an argument is an unknown flag or not an integer.
acceptance: One or more integer arguments print their sum.
Negative integers are accepted as ordinary addends.
`--help` prints the usage message and exits 0.
`--version` prints the package name and version from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` and exits 0.
An unknown flag or an argument that is not an integer prints usage and exits non-zero.
A sum that would overflow `i64` prints a short error and exits non-zero instead of panicking.
Unit tests cover sums, negative values, help, version, unknown flags, invalid input, and overflow.
constraints: Start from the reference template; keep its package metadata and lock file valid.
Tests must not touch the filesystem.
non_goals: No floats, flags other than `--help` and `--version`, stdin input, or multiple operations.
context: The reference template at `templates/bin/` is the starting point.
This is the third task in the `sum-cli` project. `tasks/sum-cli` and `tasks/sum-cli-nary` are the prior runs; their review lessons are in `lessons/sum-cli.md` and `lessons/sum-cli-nary.md`.
The prior tasks excluded overflow handling and flags; this task keeps the overflow error and adds the two flags.

compiles.reason: cargo check: error: character literal may only contain one codepoint

revision_guidance: cargo check fails on character literals in the tests. Replace every single-quoted literal with a double-quoted string literal: vec!['-1'.to_string(), "-1".to_string()] becomes vec!["-1".to_string(), "-1".to_string()]; do the same for '--help' and '--version'. Change nothing else.

handling edge cases, such as very large.text: Handling edge cases, such as very large or small numbers, can enhance the robustness of the application.

keep the dependencies minimal to adhere.text: Keep the dependencies minimal to adhere to the constraints.

remember to use `cargo clippy` to catch.text: Remember to use `cargo clippy` to catch potential warnings and improve code quality.

unit tests are crucial for validating bo.text: Unit tests are crucial for validating both valid and invalid inputs.
